editor: Vix Editor 0.1.45 command line, run offline in a no-network namespace
loader: Vix Loader 0.5.0 (Windows), driver registry override value 'vbios' in the GPU's display class key; applies after a restart

images.name: 700w-rvo
images.note: meant to let a runtime tool (mVolt+) apply voltage offsets again on driver 621.x; mVolt+ v0.50.13 --nvvdd-offsets 0,25,25 on driver 621.24 returned success with rail_offsets_ignored_by_driver=true, nvvdd_max stayed 1120 mV (18 Nov 19:20 UTC)

images.name: 700w-rel1150
images.loaded: 2026-11-18 19:20 UTC, applied at the next restart; running image verified byte for byte
images.note: raises the NVVDD REL floor above the chip's computed Vrel (1120 mV); mVolt+ --status after the restart: nvvdd_max 1170 mV (REL 1150 + ALT 20). Under load the voltage tops out at about 1.135 V read (about 1.145 V set). An earlier note here said light loads only; heavy loads use the higher limit too (19 and 20 Nov, see nvvdd_rel_floor_1150 below)

results.power.max_limit: 700.00 W after the restart; 600.00 W again after unload and restart
results.rel_ceiling_1150: no measurable effect. Afterburner's extended report (data/afterburner-report.json) shows NVVDD Vrel 1120 mV and MSVDD Vrel 1070 mV; an earlier note here said the chip's NVVDD REL was about 1070 mV, which mixed up the rails
results.msvdd_floor_1100: GT2 hang rate 4 of 9 (one hard freeze) vs 5 of 8 without; not a fix. HWiNFO still read MSVDD at 1.07 to 1.09 V under load with it loaded
results.stock_vbios_600w: Profile 1 hard-hung on GT2 run 1: the override is not the cause of the hangs
results.nvvdd_rel_floor_1150: core voltage limit 1120 -> 1170 mV; light 720p TSE GT1 3172-3195 MHz at 1.055-1.06 V before, up to 3360-3382 MHz at 1.135 V with the curve top ramped +255; 4K TSE GT1 (about 540 W) stayed at or under 1.02 V in one run on 18 Nov. The conclusion first written here, that heavy loads are unaffected, was wrong: on 19 Nov heavy loads climbed to 1.065 to 1.08 V (QUIRKS Q28), and on 20 Nov a direct test of the curve top on this image showed heavy loads at 1.03 to 1.06 V with a raised top against about 0.98 V with a flat top
results.raised_top_cost_20_nov: same image, one variable (curve top raised to 3440 MHz at 1150 mV against flat at 3090 MHz), 5 runs each, alternating: the raised top buys 1.6 to 2.8 % more fps in TSE GT1, GT2 and Steel Nomad for 79 to 114 W more mean power; peaks 620 to 668 W against at most 595 W (card's own readings). An earlier claim in these notes that this image costs about 45 W in heavy loads for no score was never tested directly and is withdrawn. The image on its own (old image against this one, same curve) is still untested. See data/raised-top-and-efficiency.json
